summary: This bill amends D.C. law to require mandatory pretrial and post-conviction detention for anyone charged with or convicted of a crime of violence or dangerous crime, and to require a secured cash bail bond for release on public safety or order offenses such as failure to appear, obstruction, rioting, or property destruction.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends DC criminal procedure statutes regarding pretrial detention and bail requirements. It contains no provisions related to federal or local government budgets, appropriations, or expenditures.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection mechanisms.
No provisions address healthcare policy, insurance, public health programs, or medical services.
The bill references existing DC firearm statutes in the context of detention presumptions but does not enact, repeal, or modify any gun regulations or restrictions.
The legislation is silent on immigration, border policy, visas, or noncitizen detention.
No content relates to reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions concern military funding, defense policy, or armed forces.
The bill does not address environmental regulations, climate policy, or natural resource management.
No changes are made to welfare programs, food assistance, or other social safety net entitlements.
The bill contains no education-related provisions.
No provisions alter drug enforcement, decriminalization, or substance-related penalties.

The bill directly reforms DC criminal procedure by mandating pretrial and post-conviction detention for crimes of violence and dangerous crimes, narrowing release options, and requiring secured cash bail for specified public safety offenses. These changes strengthen detention requirements and limit judicial discretion for release, aligning with tougher sentencing and policing approaches.
No trade, tariff, or globalization provisions are present.
The bill does not address deficit spending, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No provisions relate to LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The legislation contains no foreign aid provisions.
No election administration, voting access, or voter ID measures are included.
The bill does not address technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance policy.
No labor, union, or employment law changes are made.
The bill does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination protections.
